newsitem.title: MEXICO: Native American group to invest $200 mln in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Native American group to invest $200 mln in Mexico.

text.p: Investors from the Kumeyaays Native American tribe in California plan to invest $200 million in joint ventures with Mexican firms, a lawyer representing the group said on Friday.

"It's a $200 million investment that would be made over a period of up to 10 years," the Kumeyaays's lawyer, Daniel Jimenez Gonzalez, told a news conference organized by the National Confederation of Chambers of Commerce, Services and Tourism.

The Kumeyaays plan to invest in industry, trade and services, including casinos if Mexican laws are changed to allow them, Jimenez said. Small- and medium-sized firms would be targeted, which would also have to include social programs, he added.
"For example, if permission were granted to open a casino in Acapulco, the business owners would have to undertake social development in surrounding indigenous communities," Jimenez said.
The Kumeyaays already own and run a casino near San Diego that employs 1,600 people.
